twoEditorFlow.scenario: Optional ceramics workshop: age, resident-or-member eligibility, guardian consent, strict UTC deadline, ordered scholarship/member/student fees
twoEditorFlow.editorSaves: Concurrent Alice and Bob saves preserved independently; stale same-editor save rejected
twoEditorFlow.discovery: Member with scholarship is admitted under both interpretations but pays $25 under Alice's policy and $0 under Bob's
twoEditorFlow.matchingApprovals: Publish v2; synthetic member-scholar registration costs $25
twoEditorFlow.freshCorrection: Alice's saved policy extends the waiver to all scholars; a second adapter review finds equivalent outcomes
twoEditorFlow.correctionApprovals: One approval holds v2; two matching approvals publish v3
preservedBehavior: Youth without guardian consent remains ineligible
Registration exactly at the strict deadline remains ineligible

additionalChecks: A key alone cannot enable live studio requests; explicit server enablement is required
The adapter independently enforces disabled live mode
Public metadata and room output do not contain the test secret
Hand-authored flat wire fixtures do not depend on the production encoder
Cyclic, forward, dangling and unreachable references are rejected
Expanded condition graphs over 128 nodes and trees over depth eight are rejected
Changed source text, unexpected rule fields, auto-approval fields and inconsistent clarification output are rejected
Incomplete or malformed provider envelopes cannot produce a review
One ambiguous interpretation prevents both editors from approving either candidate
Different deadline inclusivity produces a witness at the exact UTC millisecond boundary
Two simultaneous review requests invoke one provider attempt
A response after a concurrent edit cannot overwrite newer jointly approved work
Manual fallback during an in-flight request preserves its review and approval
CAS callback replay does not duplicate model attempts
Failures preserve drafts and require explicit retries
Lease expiry is checked at application time and after CAS retry
Five external attempts per room are permitted; a sixth is refused, including when earlier attempts failed
Offline simulation has explicit provenance, needs no key and uses zero external-call budget
Offline simulation rejects ordinary rooms or altered fixture wording
limitations: This demonstrates software orchestration and validation using controlled model responses, not live Meta semantic quality or latency
The two editors are simulated roles, not independent human users
The fee correction is a new editor draft followed by another interpretation, not automatic repair synthesis
The five-attempt limit applies per room and is not an account-wide monetary spending cap
